record_id.rationale: Socrata row id: unique in all 5000 profiled rows, and the only per-row key in the source. Row grain is one invoice payment. Reviewer should confirm it persists across re-downloads; if it does not, switch to row_hash.

mappings.rationale: Only 56.5% of values carry a company suffix. Others such as 'ADACAS', 'FINITY CONSULTING' and 'ARJOHUNTLEIGH' look like trading names or short forms, so this is ambiguous between registered and trading name. collapse_ws is needed because some values contain embedded newlines (e.g. 'AMERICAN EXPRESS AUSTRALIA\nLIMITED').
Spaced 11-digit ABNs ('86 004 651 512'), 99.5% pass the real checksum. The ~0.5% that fail are dropped as parse errors, not emitted.
Derived only from unambiguous legal suffixes (PTY LTD, LIMITED, INC), otherwise unknown. Names without a suffix stay unknown, which is the ontology default. No other column states entity type.

unmapped_source_fields.reason: Socrata row-version metadata, not a claim about the business.
Socrata load timestamp, not when the publisher stated the claim. It is the same value for ~99.8% of rows, so it is no use as observed_at.
Socrata row update timestamp, not a per-record statement time. Left to the engine's resource last-modified default for observed_at.
The government payer, not an attribute of the supplier. Captured as a relationship instead.
Free-text spend category or description of the purchase (e.g. 'CONTRACTORS'). It is not an ANZSIC industry code and does not describe the supplier's industry.

Date the invoice was paid. It does not say when the supplier's name or ABN became true or stopped being true, so it must not feed valid_from/valid_to. It is also not the time the source stated the claim, since publication follows up to ~21 days after month end. No canonical field in the subset fits.
Invoice event date, empty for ~32% of rows. It is not a validity date for any entity claim.
Transaction amount (string). No canonical field in the ontology subset.
Contract reference, populated in only 0.5% of rows. No canonical field; could support linking to the ACT Contracts Register later.

unmapped_canonical_fields.reason: No ACN column. Deriving it from the last 9 ABN digits is unreliable for non-companies (sole traders, trusts, associations), so it is not derived here.
Not present; this is an ACT source.
Cannot tell which supplier_name values are trading names. Left unmapped to avoid duplicating the ambiguous name into both fields.
Receiving a payment says nothing about registration status. Default is unknown.
Not present; publish_description is a spend category, not ANZSIC.
No supplier address in the source.
No supplier address in the source.
No supplier address in the source.
No supplier address in the source.
No address data. The ontology default AU applies; no constant is asserted here since supplier location is not stated.
No per-record column states when the source made the claim. The engine falls back to the resource's last-modified date.
No column says when the supplier claim became true.
No column says when the supplier claim stopped being true.

relationships.note: ACT Government entity that paid the supplier (e.g. AHD, ACTIA). This is a customer/payer relationship, not a parent or agent of the supplier. It is a short code or name, not a registry-resolved entity.

source_reliability.rationale: Statutory ACT Government publication under the Government Procurement Act, and ABNs are largely checksum-valid. Supplier names are free text from agency finance systems and are not guaranteed to match the ABR registered name, so this is not higher.

notes: Grain is invoice payments, not businesses. Suppliers repeat (e.g. one hospital supplier has 550 of 5000 profiled rows). Expect many observations per supplier; deduplicate and resolve downstream, not at ingest.

supplier_name has 569 distinct values against 468 distinct ABNs, so the same ABN appears under several name variants. Treat the ABN as the stronger identifier and the name as a lower-confidence claim.
Licence in the dataset metadata is 'Other', which is unclear. Record observation.licence as 'unknown' and flag it for review; check the ACT Open Data terms before downstream use.

Several profiler pattern hits are coincidences, not signals: payment_amount 'acn_checksum_valid' 0.1%, publish_description 'date_like' 3.5%, contract_number 'postcode_like' 4%. None of these columns are mapped.
The dataset description is truncated, so caveats about date_invoice_received and other fields may be missing. No mapping depends on them.
File is ~55 MB / 127k rows. The root is a JSON list, so no records_path is needed; the extractor should stream it.
Fields supplier_name and supplier_abn were 100% populated in the profiled sample. If blank ABNs appear in the full file, they simply produce no abn observation.
